A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cryoSENSE work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison after matching renumbered sections and reformatted displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on five EMPIAR datasets, including image-quality measurements, 3D reconstruction, conformational heterogeneity, atomic modelling, and supplementary noise experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds pose-estimation results, a DMPlug comparison, PSNR results, and an SNR-dependent robustness evaluation.

M1.justification: The measurement operators, DCT/WT/TV reconstruction procedures, DDPM architecture, and Nesterov-guided posterior sampling remain unchanged. Section 2 and Algorithm 1 match across versions, as do the corresponding implementation appendices.

E1.justification: The same five EMPIAR datasets and biological tasks remain. v3 modestly extends coverage on EMPIAR-10076 through explicit pose-estimation evaluation and severe measurement-noise scenarios spanning 30 to -20 dB.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates DMPlug against cryoSENSE-DDPM on conformational heterogeneity and atomic modelling in Table S-5; v1 only cited DMPlug. The original comparisons among sparse priors, DDPM, and original-image controls are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds CryoSPARC homogeneous-refinement evaluation with median angular and translational errors, plus a noise-sweep protocol calibrated to measurement variance for comparable SNR across masking operators. Existing splits and training budgets remain unchanged. The stated fixed-noise setting changes from σ² = 0.1 to σ² = 0.01, but v3 figure captions instead state σ = 0.01; the actual setting and whether those experiments were rerun remain unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's compression, masking, and fixed-noise analyses, v3 tests pose-recovery robustness and systematically examines degradation across calibrated SNR levels (Table 3 and Fig. S-17). These substantially extend the investigation of practical failure conditions and differences between sparse and generative priors.

E5.justification: Both versions report reconstruction means and standard deviations using 16 validation images. The new SNR plot follows that existing image-level uncertainty practice. No additional seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Table 3's original FSC/VC values are unchanged. v3 adds pose errors, PSNR curves, SNR-dependent findings, and DMPlug outcomes. For example, Table S-5 reports DMPlug's 28 matched chains and 2.75 Å RMSD against retained DDPM results of 42 and 2.34 Å. Figure S-11 also revises the EMPIAR-11526 LPIPS/SSIM curves. These are additions and revisions to reported evidence, not an established performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: The inverse-problem definitions, sparse objectives, diffusion/posterior derivation, masking equations, and momentum formulas are retained. Appendix K.5 supplies standard SNR and noise-calibration formulas for evaluation, without adding a substantive theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same computational framework, sparse-versus-generative tradeoffs, compression limits, and biological-preservation claims. The conclusion's added wording 'computational realization' reiterates a qualification already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes existing experimental image noise from subsequently added measurement noise and explains why noise must be calibrated across operators. It also attributes DMPlug's poorer structural recovery to missing compressed-measurement consistency and interprets the new robustness results. The main micrograph-scale and hardware limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix K.5 adds concrete masking configurations, measurement variances, and noise-calibration ranges. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and preprocessing details are retained. v3 removes v1's explicit statement that code, weights, and reproduction instructions accompany the anonymous supplement, while retaining the project website; actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Punjani et al.'s cryoSPARC and Robinson et al.'s compressive 4D-STEM work. The previously cited DMPlug becomes an explicit downstream comparator and a point of differentiation concerning measurement consistency. The broader novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the Introduction–Method–Experiments–Discussion sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanations, acknowledgments, author-header edits, and appendix relabeling. v3 also duplicates the dataset-details section as Appendices G and I.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with substantial resizing and relocation of retained figures and tables. Table 3 gains pose-error columns, Table S-5 and Fig. S-17 are added, and Figs. S-8–S-15 are redrawn with PSNR panels and reorganized displays.

improvement.justification: The pose-refinement checks and variance-calibrated SNR sweep strengthen empirical support beyond v1's supplied-pose reconstructions and single stated noise level. The DMPlug comparison adds useful downstream evidence. These gains are bounded by sparse baseline implementation details, conflicting σ/σ² reporting, and editorial duplication, so the revision supports a limited overall improvement.
